A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sMBR research, with matching methods, experiments and appendices A–G. Text, equations, tables and rendered figures support reliable comparison, including v4's additional appendices H–I.

before.justification: v3 reports original translation experiments, quasi-source analyses, sensitivity studies and decoding-time measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and additionally reports GPT-4 versus T5 paraphrase-generation experiments and diverse-beam-search experiments in Tables 12–14.

M1.justification: v4 newly presents evaluated variants using GPT4-0125 instead of T5 for paraphrasing and diverse beam search instead of ordinary beam search for back-translation. These change quasi-source generation procedures, while the main implementation and source-averaged QE selection objective remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The training datasets, translation directions, resource conditions and test coverage are retained. Appendices H–I use existing high-resource En→Ru and En→De settings; changing the quasi-source generator does not introduce a new task or population.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain MAP, QE reranking and the same MBR configurations; the efficiency comparison also retains MBR-fast. The new appendix comparisons examine variants of the proposed method, without adding an independent baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4.1.3 replaces MetricX-XXL, citing MetricX-23, with MetricX-24-Hybrid-XXL. Appendices H–I add generator-choice and search-procedure comparisons within retained settings. Existing data splits, translation models and candidate budgets remain unchanged; newly supplied prompts document existing experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix H adds a targeted comparison of T5 and GPT-4 paraphrases, measuring translation quality, Self-BLEU and semantic similarity. Appendix I tests whether diverse beam search improves sMBR-BT. These extend the existing investigation of quasi-source quality and diversity; earlier sensitivity and efficiency analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use paired bootstrap significance tests with the same thresholds and no multiple-testing correction, and report timing means over five runs. Changed significance markers are result changes. The new GPT-4 nondeterminism discussion supplies no additional run counts, seed specifications or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: MetricX evidence is replaced throughout the principal comparisons and sensitivity analyses, changing rankings and significance outcomes. In Table 2, En→De's best MetricX result changes from sMBR-BT at 2.34 to sMBR-PP at 2.44 under different evaluators, so this is not a direct performance gain. Existing comparison rows retain their BLEU and XCOMET values. Tables 12–14 add results favoring GPT-4 over T5 and showing only small DBS gains over ordinary beam search, still below QE reranking.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, assumptions and complexity reasoning are retained. Appendix F rewrites Equation 13 using set notation and replaces N and M with corresponding cardinalities; the average-utility calculation is equivalent. No substantive theorem, proof or derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the source-only novelty claim and the central claims about sMBR outperforming QE reranking and standard MBR. The conclusion adds specific GPT-4 and diverse-beam-search research directions without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix H interprets the GPT-4 results as further support for surface diversity and explains retaining T5 because of reproducibility and future-access concerns. Appendix I links limited back-translation diversity to ordinary beam search and discusses the remaining performance gap. The existing main limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices A and E newly disclose the paraphrasing input/target template and exact translation prompts for all three LLM directions. Appendix H identifies GPT4-0125, although its prompt and the DBS controls remain unspecified. Existing training details, hardware disclosures and the promise to release code are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds references for GPT-4, diverse beam search and the WMT24 metrics evaluation, and replaces the MetricX-23 reference with MetricX-24. The related-work section and the central positioning of source-only MBR remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 expands future-work discussion, adds appendices H–I and prompt blocks, and standardizes some notation. Most prose and section organization are retained. New editorial errors include an sMBR-PP heading for Appendix I's sMBR-BT study and missing or incorrect appendix references.

P2.justification: v4 adds three small tables, redraws Figure 3 with updated MetricX curves and axes and a repositioned legend, and relocates that figure. Table headers and captions adopt cardinality notation, and Tables 4–5 shift position. The overall layout and Figures 1–2 are retained.

improvement.justification: Exact prompts in Appendices A and E improve reproducibility, while H–I provide useful evidence about generator choice, including DBS's continued inferiority to QE reranking. These gains outweigh localized heading and cross-reference errors, although the new variants lack complete implementation settings. The MetricX replacement does not resolve the retained concern about relying on automatic evaluation, so the overall improvement is limited.
